design_tells: pair_01: Left fuze head is a plain box with a flat overhanging cap and no striker pins/hinge detail; pull ring is a thin, oversized wire loop on a tiny eyelet instead of a thick ring on a chunky pin; spoon is a thin strip; wear is light specks instead of heavy edge chipping and bronze scratches.

pair_02: Right top is a simple rectangular block with no hinge/lever mechanism; paint wear is fine white specks and the top rim of the body has a bright bare-metal band; the inner canister reads as a smooth egg rather than a scratched cylinder.

pair_03: Left has a plain block head, a large thin wire ring on a small eyelet, and a thin wire-like spoon; smooth low-contrast paint with white specks vs. heavily chipped, textured paint and a broad stamped spoon on the right.

pair_04: Right has a bright silver worn band around the top of the green body, a thin wire ring hanging over the front, and softer, sparser wear; left spoon has a hinge-curl top and dense edge chipping.

pair_05: Left head is a plain slab with a flat cap, ring is a thin faceted wire on a small split-ring eyelet, and the green shoulder has a broad blotchy silver bare-metal band; right has a pin boss, lever hinge knuckle, thick ring, and chipped edges.

pair_06: Right head lacks the striker hook, pins and ring-pin boss; thin wire ring on a tiny eyelet; shoulder has a smeared silver wear band; paint wear is white flecks rather than chipped dark metal showing through.

pair_07: Left spoon is a smooth, soft-shaded strip with blurry grime; right spoon has a fine diamond/knurl stamp pattern, crisp chipped edges and bronze scratches, and the body paint is more heavily chipped.
pair_08: Right has a stepped double collar ring and a smooth silver worn bevel on the body shoulder; left has a chamfered collar with striped dark bevel, crisp chips, and hammered/textured paint.

pair_09: Left paint is flat, smooth olive with white specks; inner canister is a smooth egg; hole rims lack chipped bare-metal edges; right has hammered texture, drips, chipped hole rims and scratched cylindrical inner can.

pair_10: Left inner part is a smooth, clean egg/ellipsoid with a single seam and polygonal hole edge; right shows a scratched cylindrical canister with a raised collar and a chipped, beveled hole rim.

pair_11: Right paint is smooth with sparse white flecks, inner can is a smooth egg shape, hole edges are thin clean cutouts; left shows textured paint, heavy chipping and scratched cylindrical internals.
pair_12: Right base face has a thin raised segmented ring with shallow notches and flat speckled wear; left has a stepped rim with deep square notches and heavy scratched edge wear.

pair_13: Left base ring is a plain cylinder with no notched cutouts at the bottom edge and a pale silver worn band on the paint above it; right has stepped notches at the bottom rim, chamfered top with chips and heavier bronze wear.
pair_14: Right shoulder rim is a bright smeared silver band, paint is smooth with white flecks, thin wire ring; left has a chipped dark chamfer, hammered paint texture and a thick ring.

pair_15: Right lever is smooth with wispy line scratches and a faint grid, ring is a thin wire on a tiny eyelet, no striker pin boss; left lever has a stamped diamond pattern, hinge knuckle with chunky ring attachment.
tells: Copy fuze head is a plain rectangular block with a flat cap, missing the striker hook, pins, hinge knuckle and ring-pin boss of the reference.
Copy pull ring is a thin, oversized wire loop on a tiny eyelet; reference ring is a thick ring on a chunky pin.
Copy has a bright, smeared silver bare-metal band on the shoulder of the green body; reference has a dark chipped chamfer.
Copy wear is fine white paint flecks on smooth, flat olive paint; reference has hammered/textured paint, dark chips with bronze scratch edges, and drips.
Copy inner canister seen through the holes is a smooth egg/ellipsoid; reference is a scratched cylinder with a collar.
Copy spoon/lever is a smooth plain strip; reference spoon has a stamped diamond pattern and crisp chipped edges.
Copy base ring lacks the notched cutouts on its bottom edge and has a thinner, flatter segmented ring on the bottom face.
Copy hole rims are clean thin cutouts; reference hole rims are beveled and chipped.

still_differs: BRASS INNER TUBE (p4 and every top-row hole): ours looks like a smooth, untextured brass egg or capsule that fills the whole hole, with a bright horizontal seam. The reference shows a narrower vertical cylinder with dark gaps on both sides, a rounded shoulder just above the seam, and pitted, grimy brass. Measured: visible brass fraction per silhouette is ours 0.024-0.073 vs ref 0.069-0.104, and brass p50 in v2 is ours (50,42,30) vs ref (79,65,44).
HOLE RIMS: the reference has a thick cut wall and a ragged, chipped bare-steel rim around every hole. Ours has a thin, clean rim, and in p4 the hole outline shows visible straight polygon facets.
SEE-THROUGH HOLES: at the limbs of v1 and v2, the side holes in ours let the background show through (open in the alpha mask). The reference's limb holes read dark and solid.

PAINT WEAR: ours is a fairly clean, even olive with small white/cream flecks. The reference has heavy dark grime blotches, brown-bronze chips and scratches all over. Bright bare fraction on the central body band: ours 0.1-1.0% vs ref 1.3-5.9%. Paint fraction of the silhouette: ours 0.52/0.58/0.52/0.41 vs ref 0.45/0.48/0.41/0.40 (v1-v4). Paint p90 is ours 91-97 vs ref 101-116, and p10 is ours 44-53 vs ref 40-44, so our paint has less contrast.
SLEEVE TOP CHAMFER: ours is an even, bright, near-chrome silver band that stands out strongly (pair 5/8/14). In the reference it is worn and patchy dark steel with a little bare metal.

FUZE HEAD shape: ours is narrower. Silhouette width at H 3.4 D, housing plus attached parts: ours 0.72-0.86 D vs ref 0.975-1.04 D. Ours is a plain box with vertical panel lines and a flat top plate that overhangs far to one side. The reference has a raised front panel with a slot, a side lug with a small curl and cross pin, a small screw or boss, and a solid round hinge knuckle.

LEVER TOP: ours bends into an open hook or curl with a visible gap around the knuckle. The reference's lever top wraps a solid, short horizontal knuckle cylinder, and the pin boss and eye sit next to it.

PULL RING: ours is thin, lighter grey, and visibly polygonal (faceted) in the p1 close-up. The reference ring is a thick, round, dark steel wire. In v2 the reference ring swings outside the right limb down to H 2.65 D; ours stays inside the limb. In v4 the reference ring stands outside the left limb from H 2.68 to 3.39 D; ours does not.

LEVER IN v1: in the reference the lever stands clear to the right of the body from H 0.77 to 3.55 D. In ours only H 2.59 to 3.55 D shows outside the limb, because the lower lever hides behind the body. At v3 the lever tip matches (0.975 D both).
LEVER FACE (pair 7): ours is smooth dark steel with only faint wear. The reference has dense diagonal scratch hatching with bright worn edges.

BASE CAP SIDE (pair 13): the reference foot has a wide stepped recess or notch cut into the lower band, plus a small notch at the top chamfer. Ours is a plain faceted band with no recess. Its steel is flatter, with weaker bright edges: cap p90 ours 56-67 vs ref 65-79.

BASE END FACE (p3, pair 12): the reference has a chunky raised rim lip with deep, blocky rectangular notches, and the central disc steps down at each notch. Ours reads as a thin engraved double ring with small shallow notches, much flatter. The reference cap is also heavily scratched with bronze wear, while ours has pale specks.
STEEL TONE: ours housing steel is lighter and flatter. Housing p50 in v2/v3 is ours 65-69 vs ref 42-50. The reference shows darker oxidised steel with sharper, brighter worn edges.
RING LINES (p2): the reference ring lines are crisp engraved grooves with a lighter lip and chipped paint along them. Ours are thin dark lines with little wear along them.

Top-row silhouette IoU against the Study's traced outlines, measured with my own alpha: v1 0.80, v2 0.88, v3 0.86, v4 0.90. Paint IoU: 0.70/0.72/0.68/0.65. Paint p50 matches within 2-6 levels (lighting calibrated: backdrop 47 vs 45).

My independent yaw search (workbench BC render, 5 deg sweep, paint IoU + silhouette IoU) chose v1 -145, v2 165, v3 -110, v4 -20. These are close to the builder's -130/170/-110/-25. v3 at 165 gave better paint IoU but worse silhouette, and the reference views still do not form one rigid turntable.
invented: The brass tube is closed as a capsule behind each hole, with a domed look and a bright horizontal seam at the middle. The reference shows an open vertical tube with a shoulder and dark gaps.
See-through limb holes: background is visible through the body at the v1/v2 limbs.
An open-hook lever curl with a gap at the top. The reference has a solid knuckle cylinder.
A long flat top plate overhanging to the ring/lever side (p1). The reference's plate is smaller, with a side lug and cross-pin curl.
Several vertical panel lines on the housing faces (normal-map detail). The reference has one raised front panel and a slot, not these lines.
A bright, even, near-polished silver band on the sleeve top chamfer.
Pale white/cream speckle chips on the paint and cap. The reference's wear is dark grime plus bronze-edged chips and scratches.
A thin engraved double-ring groove on the base end face in place of the reference's chunky raised notched lip.
maker.summary:
I rendered the shipped SM_Flashbang.fbx (LOD0) with only its shipped maps, T_Flashbang_BC/ORM/N (DirectX green flipped), using my own headless Blender 5.2 script: WorkFiles/flashbang/measure_r1/mr_render.py.

Top row: one ~74.6 mm (2600 px) camera with the horizon at row 460 photographs four copies. Each copy's axis is placed on the reference body centre and its foot on the contact row. The per-view yaws come from my own Workbench yaw sweep scored by paint and silhouette IoU (v1 -145, v2 165, v3 -110, v4 -20). The backdrop is a dark emissive-diffuse sweep with a soft key from the upper right and front, calibrated to a background p50 of 47 vs the reference's 45 and paint p50 within a few levels. The four close-ups p1-p4 were framed by eye over five iterations; p4 uses depth of field.

Outputs in measure_r1: mr_eight_views.png, mr_side_by_side.png, mr_close_side.png, mr_row_alpha.png and mr_measure.json (element metrics).

Blind test: 16 pairs, reference vs ours at identical pixel boxes and scale, sides chosen at random with secrets. The key was checked against the pixel data and exists only in key_ours_side. The PNGs are hand-written with only the IHDR, IDAT and IEND chunks (no metadata) in the new folder WorkFiles/flashbang/blind_r1/.
- Pairs 1-4: the four views.
- 5: fuze head (p1).
- 6: ring and pin (v1 head).
- 7: lever and tip (v4).
- 8: top collar and sleeve (v2).
- 9: hole rows and spacing (v2).
- 10: inner brass tube (p4).
- 11: ring line (p2).
- 12: notched base face (p3).
- 13: cap side and foot (v3).
- 14: paint wear and chipping (v1 sleeve and row A).
- 15: steel finish (v4 head and collar).
- 16: silhouette masks (the Study's outer outlines vs our filled alpha).

Verdict: the overall proportions, the three aligned hole rows, the cap and sleeve bands and the v3 lever tip match well. It would likely still fail a blind test on sight:
- The brass tube reads as a smooth capsule, not a textured vertical tube.
- The paint and steel wear is too clean, with white specks, weak grime and a chrome-like sleeve chamfer.
- The fuze head is narrower and simpler (open-hook lever curl, big flat plate).
- The ring is thin and faceted.
- The base face notches and the foot recess are too shallow or missing.
- The limb holes are see-through.

No Blender or Unreal process was left running. Nothing outside WorkFiles/flashbang/measure_r1 and WorkFiles/flashbang/blind_r1 was written, and no frozen, pack or other-chat files were touched.

craft_issues.area: Fuze head: housing, top plate and hinge
craft_issues.issue: The housing is a plain narrow box: the width at H 3.4 D is 0.72-0.86 D against the reference's 0.975-1.04 D. It has vertical normal-map panel lines and a large thin top plate overhanging 8.4 mm to one side (it reads as a lid in fuze_yaw60 and yaw180). The reference's raised front panel with a slot, the side lug with its small curl and cross pin, the small screw boss and the solid round hinge knuckle are missing. At hand distance this is the first thing the eye lands on.
craft_issues.fix: Rebuild the head as real geometry. Add a raised front panel about 1 mm proud with a vertical slot. On the ring side add a side lug with a curl around a cross pin of about 2 mm diameter. Add a solid knuckle cylinder of 0.137 D diameter by 0.33 D length, a pin-boss cylinder (0.095 D diameter by 0.17 D) on the side next to the knuckle, and a small screw head. Shorten the top plate to at most 0.07-0.1 D of overhang. Delete the panel-line strokes from the detail normal. Register a head crop at H 3.0-3.8 D against v1-v4 and require head silhouette width within 5% of the reference in each view.

craft_issues.issue: The top of the lever bends into an open hook with a visible gap around the knuckle, plus an S-crank at the joggle (craft_fuze_yaw180, fp_yaw150). The plate is a flat 2.2 mm strip, so seen edge-on (v1, and the first-person yaw150 view) it reads as a thin wire or strap. In the reference the edge-on lever is clearly deep, about 0.08 D (roughly 3.5 mm), and wraps a solid knuckle. The lever face is smooth with low-frequency cloudy mottling where the reference has dense diagonal stamped hatching and bright worn edges.
craft_issues.fix: Close the curl tightly around the solid knuckle (inner radius = knuckle radius + 0.3 mm, no gap). Replace the crank with a single smooth joggle step at 3.29 D. Give the lever a shallow channel section: an 11.4 mm web with 3-3.5 mm flanges, or at least a 3.5 mm-thick look using bevelled edges, so the edge-on view has mass. Paint a diagonal cross-hatch scratch pattern (two directions about ±35 deg, 0.2-0.4 mm lines at about 1.5 mm spacing) and bright arris wear on the flange edges. In v1 the lever must stand clear of the right limb from H 0.77 to 3.55 D, which it does not now (only 2.59 to 3.55 D); pick the v1 yaw or lever standoff to satisfy this.

craft_issues.area: Brass inner tube and hole interiors
craft_issues.issue: Through every hole the tube reads as a smooth, clean brass egg with a bright horizontal seam, because the ceiling and floor of the gap show as dark curved edges. The reference shows a straight vertical cylinder with dark gaps on both sides, a small shoulder above the seam, and pitted, grimy brass. The brass island in the BC is a flat, untextured tan block. Visible brass fraction is 0.024-0.073 against the reference's 0.069-0.104, and brass p50 in v2 is (50,42,30) against (79,65,44). The limb holes in v1 and v2 are see-through to the background; the reference limbs read dark.
craft_issues.fix: Move the gap's ceiling and floor discs so they sit behind the webs between rows and are never visible through a hole. Model a 0.5 mm shoulder step just above the seam in each row. Paint the brass with pitting, dark grime in the lower third, vertical anisotropic scratches, and roughness around 0.35-0.5 with variation. Darken the gap with AO (painted into BC if needed) so the two dark side slivers read. Close the line of sight at the limbs, either with a dark inner liner at about r 19.5 mm or with dark end rings. Gate: zero background pixels through the body in the v1-v4 alpha, and brass fraction per view within ±20% of the reference.

craft_issues.area: Hole walls and rims: UVs, facets, chrome ring
craft_issues.issue: In T_Flashbang_BC the hole-wall faces are unwrapped inside the paint islands and stretched radially. They form X-shaped starburst streaks around every hole, and in the renders every hole wall is one continuous bright silver ring (fp crops, fuze_yaw60, base). The rim is thin and clean where the reference has a thick cut wall with a ragged, chipped bare-steel rim. In the N map the hole bevels show wedge-shaped rainbow facets, and the p4 macro shows straight polygon edges. LOD2 holes are octagons.
craft_issues.fix: Unwrap each hole wall as its own unrolled strip island at the atlas texel density (8.7 px/mm). Paint the walls dark steel with grime; the painted outer surface should come to a 0.5-1.5 mm irregular chipped bare rim, driven by noise, not a uniform band. Raise the hole ring to at least 20-24 segments at LOD0 and 12 at LOD2. Pay for the triangles by cutting segments on the hidden brass tube faces, gap discs and top plate, keeping LOD0 at or under 6,000. Re-bake the bevel normal after re-segmenting.

craft_issues.issue: The paint is a fairly clean, even olive with small white or cream flecks. The reference has heavy dark grime blotches, brown-bronze chips with dark steel showing through, drips or hammered texture, and scratches. Bright bare fraction on the central band is ours 0.1-1.0% against the reference's 1.3-5.9%. Paint p90 is 91-97 against 101-116, and p10 is 44-53 against 40-44, so the tonal range is too narrow at both ends. Paint fraction of the silhouette is ours 0.52/0.58/0.52/0.41 against the reference's 0.45/0.48/0.41/0.40.
craft_issues.fix: Change the chip colour model rather than tuning numbers. A chip core should be dark oxidised steel (sRGB about 45-60) with a thin bright bronze-to-steel edge (sRGB about 110-140, warm), not a flat pale fill. Add a large-scale grime layer (dark brown-black blotches of 3-15 mm, 10-15% coverage, collecting near rims, ring lines and the base) and a hammered or orange-peel low-amplitude normal on the paint. Add fine scratch strokes in the paint. Re-solve so paint p10, p50 and p90 each land within ±5 levels of the reference, and the bright bare fraction on the central band is 1.5-5%.

craft_issues.area: Sleeve top chamfer and base-cap top chamfer
craft_issues.issue: Both chamfers read as continuous bright, near-chrome silver bands. This is the blind panel's number-one tell (pairs 5, 8 and 14) and is even more obvious at first-person distance: fp_yaw30 and yaw150 show a white ring at the shoulder and above the cap. In the reference the sleeve chamfer is worn, patchy, dark steel with some paint still on it and only broken bright spots.
craft_issues.fix: Keep paint on 50-70% of the sleeve chamfer and break it with the chip mask. Where bare, use dark steel (roughness 0.45-0.6) with bright arris wear on at most 20-30% of the length, in broken dashes. Apply the same to the cap's top chamfer. Gate: mean luminance of the chamfer band within ±10 levels of the reference crop in v2 and v3.

craft_issues.issue: The ring is a thin (1.76 mm), light grey, visibly faceted wire hanging from a small secondary split-ring eyelet (fuze_yaw-60, p1). The reference ring is a thicker, dark steel wire that passes through the eye of a chunky pin boss. In v2 the reference ring swings outside the right limb down to H 2.65 D, and in v4 it stands outside the left limb from H 2.68 to 3.39 D; ours does neither. At LOD1 and LOD2 the ring becomes a 12-gon (flashbang_lods.png).
craft_issues.fix: Use a wire of about 2.2-2.5 mm and a darker, antiqued steel (base sRGB about 60-75, roughness 0.4) with bright wear only on the outer arc. Remove the extra eyelet ring and pass the ring through a hole in the end of the pin-boss cylinder. Use at least 32 segments around the loop and 8 around the wire at LOD0; 20 by 6 at LOD1; 12 by 4 at LOD2. Keep the same centreline at every LOD. Re-pose the ring so it hangs outward (about 25-35 deg off the sleeve) to match the limb overhangs in v2 and v4.

craft_issues.area: Base cap end face and foot
craft_issues.issue: The end face reads as a thin engraved double ring with small, shallow notches (craft_base, pair 12). The reference has a chunky raised rim lip with deep, blocky rectangular notches, and the central disc steps down at each notch. The side foot recess seen in v1 and v3 is missing, so from the side the cap is a plain faceted band (pair 13). The cap steel is flat with pale specks: cap p90 is 56-67 against 65-79.
craft_issues.fix: Model the lip 1.5-2 mm proud with a width of about 3 mm. Cut the 5 notches (about 4-5 mm wide) through the full lip height and out through the outer bottom edge, and add a 1 mm step down on the central disc. Notches that exit the outer edge also show from the side as small rectangular cut-outs at the foot, which reconciles the close-up with the v1/v2/v3 side views; verify against those crops. Paint the cap with heavy scratches, bronze-tinted wear on the edges and grime in the recesses, and raise the bright-edge contrast until cap p90 is 65-79.

craft_issues.issue: At the shipped 0.889 m switch (90 deg hfov, 1080p) the LOD0-to-LOD1 diff concentrates on the ring outline and the housing top (craft_lodpop_889.png): 5.1% of object pixels change by more than 20/255 and p99 is 62. The whole ring outline lights up, so the ring's path or shape changes, not just its tessellation. At 2.538 m, LOD1-to-LOD2 changes 21% of pixels by more than 20 (p99 136) around the ring, the hinge and the housing top. The octagonal holes at LOD2 are visible in the LOD sheet. The builder's p99 surface-deviation metric of 0.34 mm hides this because it ignores the ring and lever silhouette shift.
craft_issues.fix: Generate every LOD's ring from the same centreline, reducing segments only as listed in the ring fix. Keep the knuckle, curl and top-plate outline identical at LOD1. Add a gate: a rendered pixel diff at each switch distance with frac(>20/255) under 2% on object pixels, measured on silhouette plus shading.

craft_issues.area: Bake artefacts in the shipped maps
craft_issues.issue: T_Flashbang_N has a solid (0.50, 0.50, 0.005) block (27,199 texels, about 170x150 px at atlas uv 0.76-0.84, 0.75-0.81). That is an inward-pointing, invalid tangent normal. It maps to two faces at z 161.5 mm, normal +Z (the housing top under the top plate, 397 mm2). It is hidden today but becomes visible if the top plate changes, and it wastes about 0.65% of the atlas. The housing's front island in the BC also carries a large vertical vesica-shaped scratch outline that reads as an odd lens engraving on the housing face (craft_fuze_yaw180, fp_yaw150 crop).
craft_issues.fix: Delete or collapse the hidden housing-top faces, or shrink their island to a few texels. Add a gate that fails if any used texel has N.B < 0.5. Cap the scratch generator's curvature and forbid closed loops, and regenerate the housing wear.

craft_issues.issue: The shipped pattern is 5 holes per row at 0/60/120/180/270 deg, which leaves a 90-deg blank web on the back. It is defensible as the only pattern that fits every inconsistent reference view, but on a hero object rotated in the hand it reads as an invented asymmetry. The front-facing views v2 and v3 are consistent with 6 evenly spaced holes, which is the natural manufactured design.
craft_issues.fix: Put the choice to the user with two renders: 6 evenly spaced holes against the current 5-uneven layout, both at the per-view yaws. If 6-even is chosen, re-run the yaw and phase search; v1 and v4 will need their own yaws, which the per-view yaw approach already allows.

craft_issues.issue: Renders/Flashbang/flashbang_back.png is empty: an 1600x900 dark gradient with no grenade in frame. It ships in Renders as if it were a back view.
craft_issues.fix: Fix the back-view camera target and distance in flashbang_gallery.py and add a check that the object covers more than 5% of the frame for every gallery render.

craft_issues.issue: The engraved ring lines are 0.66 mm normal-only detail. At hand distance they read as seams between three stacked drums, with no lighter lip and no chipped paint along them. The reference shows crisp engraved grooves with a lighter upper lip and paint chipped along the line.
craft_issues.fix: Model each ring line as a real V-groove (0.6-0.8 mm wide, 0.4 mm deep; about 2 extra loops per line, which is cheap). Add a bright lip highlight via the bevel bake and bias the chip mask so chips run along the groove.

applied: I rebuilt from scratch with Scripts/props/build_flashbang.py (library 2.0.0). All 23 build gates pass (round 1 had 19); the four new ones are no invalid normal texel, no background visible through the body at any LOD, LOD pop, and gallery coverage. qa_check passes 88/88, 84/84, 71/71 and 71/71. Round 1's scripts, exports and renders are backed up in WorkFiles/flashbang/fin/r1_backup/.

README defect (major): Exports/Flashbang/README.md import step 1 now lists the ASSET_GUIDELINES 6.5 settings: Convert Scene ON, Force Front XAxis OFF, Convert Scene Unit ON, Uniform Scale 1.0, Import Normals with MikkTSpace, Import Mesh LODs ON, One Convex Hull per UCX, Auto Collision OFF and Generate Lightmap UVs ON. It also says what goes wrong with the defaults. MATERIALS_README.md was rewritten: default colour #494932, Lightest Colour #CBCBCB, Metal From ORM behaviour.

The 8-bit Paint_Detail (it built as BGRA8, 21.9 MB) is no longer shipped. It is now only the build-work source of the lossless Recolour/T_Flashbang_Paint_Detail16.png. recolour_maps.json lists only the recolourable Paint part; the Steel slot moved to other_slots so np_spec can resolve it.

Fuze head: added a raised front panel on the -X face, 1 mm proud, split by a vertical slot. Cut the top-plate overhang from 8.4 to 4.0 mm (0.09 D) and made the plate cover the housing. Removed the hidden housing top face that had baked an invalid normal. The knuckle now fills the lever curl between the lever's flanges. The pin head is a thick cylinder (r 2.3 x 4.2 mm) that the ring passes through; the split-ring eyelet is gone.

Lever: now a channel section (1.3 mm sheet with 3.3 mm flanges toward the body), so it has depth edge-on. Around the knuckle the flanges form the hinge cheeks, which closes the open hook. The S-crank is replaced by one straight diagonal joggle with 1.4 mm fillets. The web face has a stamped +-35 deg cross-hatch at 1.5 mm pitch, broken up, with dashed bright arris wear.

Brass 'egg': the inside is rebuilt as one brass can per hole column (r 5.7 mm, narrower than the hole), so each hole shows a vertical lit cylinder with dark gaps on both sides. Added dark radial dividers and dark top and bottom discs. The brass is brighter and pitted, with vertical scratches, grime in the lower third, and a seam groove with a lighter shoulder band. See-through is 0 px in all four views at LOD0, LOD1 and LOD2; at LOD2 the dividers run out to the skin.
Holes: the walls are now dark cut steel with grime (the old bright 0.42 metal was the chrome ring). Holes have 24 / 18 / 16 points per LOD (was 20 / 10 / 8).

Paint: new wear model. Chips have a dark oxidised core with a thin warm bright edge (from an eroded chip mask) and are 1-3 mm blotches. Grime blotches of 3-15 mm cover 17 % of the paint at the rims, ring lines, base and step. Added lighter scuffs, a hammered paint normal and thin bright scratches through the paint. The sleeve chamfer keeps most of its paint. Steel arrises are bright only on the thin bevel, in noise-broken dashes. Scratches are now straight strokes, which removes the lens-shaped mark on the housing. Steel is darker, with short scratch strokes and bronze specks.

Pull ring: 2.4 mm dark antiqued wire, bright only on the outer arc, hanging 30 deg off the sleeve. Segments are 32x8 / 24x8 / 24x8 on one centreline, with polygon radii set so the perimeter matches the true circle.

Base cap: the end face is rebuilt with a recessed disc, a groove, a wide contact rim and 5 blocky inward notches (5 mm). The same notches are cut 2 mm up through the outer foot edge, giving the side views' foot cut-outs; they are real geometry with wall triangles.

LOD pop: LOD1 keeps 18-point holes, 8-segment cans, the ring and the disc/groove/rim. I added a rendered gate (90 deg hfov, 1080p, 3 turns, alpha-masked, with a same-LOD other-seed noise floor). Worst change is now 0.27 % at 0.889 m and 0.67 % at 2.54 m (round 1: 5.1 % and 21 %).

Maps: any used texel whose baked normal points inward is replaced by a flat normal (159 texels) and gated. The back render now turns the object instead of the camera, with a coverage gate. The hero is framed closer.

Pack materials: I took the lock as flashbang-chat and added items Flashbang, Flashbang_Body, Flashbang_PullRing and Flashbang_Lever to material_spec.json. They share MI_Flashbang_Paint (M_Fabric_Master with Metal From ORM) and MI_Flashbang_Steel (M_Steel_Master); the ORM uses the NormalRoughnessToGreen composite, as on the sheath and heels.
